stem.text: Rain falls at a rate of r(t) millimeters per hour, where r is differentiable and t is measured in hours. Measured values are r(0) = 3, r(2) = 5, r(4) = 4, r(6) = 2. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{6} r(t)\,dt \), the total rainfall, in millimeters, from t = 0 to t = 6, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 2 \cdot \frac{3 + 5}{2} = 8 \); \( 2 \cdot \frac{5 + 4}{2} = 9 \); \( 2 \cdot \frac{4 + 2}{2} = 6 \).

distractor_derivations.A: trapezoid area taken as width times the sum of the two endpoint values, with no division by 2
distractor_derivations.B: factor 1/2 applied to the last trapezoid only
distractor_derivations.C: right Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
